statements.t: We are setting units and quoting additional projects with these customers.

Last quarter, we said we would revisit our guidance once we had a full quarter of Flatrock, that we expected to add 55,000 horsepower organically this year and that we had more to do to put underutilized assets to work.
Today, we are raising our full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance.
We remain on track for 55,000 horsepower,
Together with the fleet management work I described earlier, we believe these investments will put NGS at the forefront of the industry in how we collect and use data.
Together, we expect these efforts to put more of our idle fleet back to work and improve returns on the fleet we already own.
Based on the opportunities we see today, I expect that to continue.
Through the third quarter, we have added approximately 43,000 horsepower organically, which keeps us on track for 55,000 horsepower for the year.
Beyond the units we continue to set with them, we are quoting new large horsepower projects.
Given equipment lead times, that work will take time to show up in our financial results, but it reflects the strength of the relationships Flatrock developed, and we intend to build on them.
It is in line with expectations and full-year guidance is only modestly above our initial 2026 range, even though the fleet is roughly 15% larger.
We will continue to evaluate opportunities based on strategic fit, customer mix, basin position, fleet characteristics, and valuation.
We do not expect prices to stay at these levels indefinitely, and our business does not depend on them.
Policy changes could reduce that to some extent, but we expect the increase to remain material.
Combined with the continued demand for gas lift on the oil side, that gives us a positive outlook.

We will continue to use pricing, operating data, and disciplined execution across procurement and our field operations to help manage those pressures while maintaining the service levels our customers expect.
We do not expect to recover every increase immediately, and lubricant inflation remains a headwind.

Looking ahead, we expect the fourth quarter to be the final period of meaningful integration-related expenses, with our remaining efforts focused on optimizing the combined cost structure to generate additional fixed cost leverage.
Consistent with our historical treatment, these expenses will be excluded from adjusted results.

With that, I'll turn the call back to Justin to discuss our updated guidance and closing comments.

Based on our third quarter results, a full quarter of Flatrock, and our organic fleet additions, we are increasing our full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $105 million to $108 million from our previous range of $103 million to $108 million.

With a full quarter of Flatrock behind us and better visibility into equipment timing, we're narrowing our full-year growth capital expenditure guidance to $60 to $75 million from $60 to $80 million, with no change to our horsepower expectations.
Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will conduct the question and answer session.
We'll have that on the fourth quarter call.
The way I would describe it is there are a meaningful number of equipment commitments through 2027, enough that I am confident 2027 will be the fifth year of market share gains for us.
And so, as we look at the growth rate going forward, without providing numbers at this point, we continue to expect it to be strong.

I’m certainly not going to attempt to forecast future inflation, but I can speak to the actions we’re taking to mitigate its impact, which I think are reflected in our year-over-year margins in the third quarter.

I think these initiatives have helped us to expand our rental gross margins despite those inflationary pressures, and we believe they do position us well to continue protecting profitability going forward.

And if that weakness persists, I think we intend to be opportunistic with our $6-million repurchase authorization, particularly when the implied multiple on forward-adjusted EBITDA offers returns comparable to our organic growth investments.

We’ve been unable to repurchase shares over the past several weeks due to the earnings blackout period, and at this point, we’re exploring a 10b5-1 plan to provide us greater flexibility going forward during these blackout periods.
Ian Eckert: Tate, I do believe we’ll still have some degree of sales, but they will be muted.

As we look out over the next several years, I went through in the market outlook what we see on the upstream side as it relates to oil, and more in the midstream as it relates to natural gas, I think the factors that are driving a very strong environment are likely to continue.
We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

statements.t: We expect the final settlement to occur in November 2026, at which time $1.9 million will be released from escrow to the Sellers with the remaining $0.4 million returned to the Company.
Regardless of current oil price volatility driven by geopolitical factors, we expect demand for compression overall, and specifically our fleet, to remain strong.

We believe the market outlook for natural gas production in the U.S. remains steady while short-term price volatility remains a factor due to geopolitical influences, weather and shifts in LNG exports.

In addition, our costs of sales include overhead and related support costs attributable to our storage and assembly facilities including the Tulsa Facility, which we expect to be sold in the fourth quarter of 2026, and the Midland, Texas facility currently held for sale through its closure at the end of March 2025.

The costs to support our sales revenues increased during the three months ended September 30, 2026, due primarily to unabsorbed overhead costs attributable to the Tulsa Facility resulting from winding down operations in advance of the expected sale.

We expect to incur additional integration expenses during the fourth quarter of 2026 including retention bonuses and severance benefits to appropriately align our support staff and incorporate the legacy Flatrock business into our ERP, human resources and compensation and benefits systems, among others.

As referenced above, we recently completed our cloud-based ERP system implementation project for which we have capitalized certain qualified costs and expensed others during 2025 and through the early part of the third quarter of 2026.
The higher horsepower unit additions are reflective of our strategic plans to concentrate our business development on these higher margin applications.

As circumstances warrant, we will market certain property and equipment, primarily trucks, when we have determined that there is no longer a productive use for such assets or favorable opportunities arise to monetize otherwise idle assets.

Our estimated annual effective tax rate differs from the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% primarily as a result of a higher effective tax rate attributable to state and local income taxes including the impact of projected apportionment of taxable income between states with different tax rates.

Our cash flows from operating and investing activities are subject to a degree of volatility due primarily to (i) the consistency of our customers in remitting amounts owed to us for our services in full and on a timely basis and (ii) the timing of payments to our vendors and suppliers for capital projects which are often made well in advance of placing new compressor equipment into service.

Our forecasted capital expenditures for the remainder of 2026 will continue to be directly dependent upon our customers’ compression requirements and our capital availability, while maintaining prudent levels of debt.

Included in these totals for 2026 and 2025 were $48.2 million and $77.9 million for growth capital expenditures to expand our rental fleet and $11.7 million and $9.1 million for capital maintenance projects, respectively.
Our investment in rental equipment includes any changes to work-in-progress related to our rental fleet projects at the beginning of the year compared to the end of the period.

As I look at the forward – obviously, we talked extensively here about the market and the growth that we see going forward, and obviously, the growth that we've achieved over the last several years.
And there are new opportunity sets in terms of customers that we think we're going to be able to capture some equipment with going forward.
And new customer wins out there, I think we'll be able to hit or be able to capture growth with them.

We're not going to set longer-term targets at this point, really going to point to our track record of materially outpacing the industry, and with what I see and what I've seen people disclose, quite comfortable in saying we'll continue to do that in the future.
We're not going to give a formal synergy target right now.
The current guidance that we've provided does not assume material labor application synergies.

We viewed this deal as an opportunity to acquire very attractive assets and a strong field service organization, and it certainly wasn't reliant on any synergies that we expect to deliver over the course of the next year.

In terms of how we're looking at the M&A landscape, it's really through the exact same kind of framework that we were using previously, and have used consistently applied in the Flatrock acquisition apply going forward.
We will look at, and have looked at, and continue to look at whole company acquisitions, partial acquisitions of competitors or customers equipment.

When I take a look at the margins for the second half of the year, we certainly don't expect the first quarter margin of 63.7% to be permanent, as you saw in the second quarter, but we do expect that the underlying fleet economics will remain strong.
Obviously, that's always a balance, but it's something we're constantly looking at and looking across the different cost buckets in what we expect in terms of inflation.
We look forward to continuing to execute and updating you on our progress next quarter.
